title: Normalize structured-output and tool-invocation metering for non-chat endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Correct and unify how we meter tokens/units and rate-limit enforcement for non-chat endpoints that perform embeddings, reranking, and function/tool invocations returning structured output. Current divergences between endpoint handlers lead to inconsistent charges (double-counting on partial failures, speculative prefetch being charged without attribution, and mismatched rate-limit token buckets per route vs per-customer), causing customer support cases and potential revenue leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical usage calculation applied to embeddings/rerank/structured-output endpoints documented and implemented in runtime
Tool-invocation calls (function/tool) produce a deterministic token/operation attribution even for partial-success and retry paths
Rate-limiter semantics defined: burst credits, per-route vs per-customer policy, and transparent quota deductions
Backfill reconciliation job created to correct historical mis-attributed charges for affected customers (sampled subset) and PRD for full rollout
Unit + integration tests covering multi-call rerank flows, speculative prefetch, forced partial failures, and idempotent replays
Telemetry + dashboard updated to surface per-invocation attribution and top N causes for meter divergence
technical_notes: Introduce a MeteringContext object propagated with each request to collect deterministic accounting events (start/stop, tokens_generated, embeddings_tokens, kd_cache_hits, tool_call_invocations)
Implement 'finalize_usage' hook in runtime that applies attribution rules in a single place; hooks invoked once even if requests trigger retries or fallbacks
Deduplicate speculative prefetch and cache-warming flows by tagging requests with prefetch=true and suppressing charge if the later real request consumes cached result within 30s
Function/tool calls must emit an invocation_id (UUID) and a status enum (ok|partial|failed). Use invocation_id to correlate charges and avoid double-billing across retries
Rate limiting: unify token bucket implementation so that per-customer limits are enforced first, then per-route; burst credits are stored in Redis with TTL and audited
Expose a debug header (X-Redwood-Meter-Debug) in canary to return a condensed accounting trace for sampled requests
Create reconciliation job 'billing-reconcile-structured-ops' to scan 90 days of events and emit corrective adjustment proposals to finance review queue
rollout_plan: Step 1 (canary): deploy MeteringContext + finalize_usage to 5% runtime nodes with X-Redwood-Meter-Debug enabled
Step 2 (validation): run synthetic test suite and 1 week of telemetry comparison vs baseline, check for >0.1% difference in total billed tokens
Step 3 (gradual ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks if no regressions and finance signoff
Step 4 (backfill): run reconciliation job in dry-run; present proposed adjustments to Finance + Legal before applying
Step 5 (customer comms): update billing docs and send targeted notices to customers affected by corrections >$100/month
